description: Per-wave story battle setup: allied MissionCharacter rows, playable-character slot, MissionWave link and battle-talk sets.

ID.simple: Story mission wave row id, normally the mission id.
ID.technical: FName row key (row +0x8) in StoryMissionWaveDataTables (DTM +0x8E0), reached through StoryMission.Id_StoryMissionWave[WaveIndex] or, in several first-wave helpers, [0]. Consumers search the loaded tables by this key; the reconstructed code does not read the row’s Id value directly. GamePhase_BattleStory builds the per-mission wave array, and FStudioBattleMissionTaskSystem::SetupStory caches the resolved rows in StoryMissionWaves with the RetryCount-selected pointer exposed as StoryMissionWave / GetStoryMissionWave. Exported row keys equal their ID values; four STMSN_09112M_0N rows are wave variants of one mission rather than separate mission ids.

Id_MissionCharacter_Ally.simple: Allied MissionCharacter rows taking part in this wave.
Id_MissionCharacter_Ally.technical: TArray<FName> (row +0x10), with three slots in every exported row. None is an empty sentinel at a retained index. Story_GetBattleLayout removes None before counting allies; Story_GetPlayableCharacterIndex counts only non-None allies for its fallback. Story_GetMissionAllyCharacters resolves each slot to a MissionCharacter row, skips unresolved and already-collected rows, and inserts the slot equal to Wave->PlayableCharacterIndex at the front of that wave’s result. Story_ResolveDemoLaunch indexes the first wave to set the player battle-character slot from the resolved playable index; SetupBattleCharacterEntries indexes the current cached wave with the runtime StudioStoryPlayableIndex_CE8 and skips None and the player slot when adding computer-controlled allies.

PlayableCharacterIndex.simple: Index in Id_MissionCharacter_Ally that the player controls.
PlayableCharacterIndex.technical: int32 (row +0x20), constructor default 0; exported values are -2 (one row), -1 (87), 0 (four) and 1 (one). Story_GetPlayableCharacterIndex returns the first wave’s raw value only when it is > -1; otherwise it returns 0 when exactly one ally is non-None and -1 for zero or multiple allies (also -1 for a missing mission/wave). Story_ResolveDemoLaunch stores that resolved index in the launch request and, when it is not -1, uses it to index the first wave’s ally array for the player battle slot. Story_HasPlayableCharacterIndex tests the first wave value > -2; false routes to character select and suppresses the extra allies in SetupBattleCharacterEntries. Story_GetMissionAllyCharacters compares the raw value against each slot index, while Story_GetBattleLayout uses the first wave’s value even for a later wave and forces the ally count to 1 when it is <= -2. Several first-wave helpers dereference [0] or GetData()[0] without a Num check, and character-select battle settings use the runtime StudioStoryPlayableIndex_CE8 rather than this field.

Id_MissionWave.simple: Generic MissionWave row for enemy/order data.
Id_MissionWave.technical: FName (row +0x24) used as the key into MissionWaveDataTables (DTM +0x9A0) by Story_GetBattleLayout, Story_GetDemoMissionTask, SetupBattleCharacterEntries and the story-mission info widget. The linked MissionWave row supplies enemy ids, layout/time/order data and Id_MissionTaskLottery, whose first task id provides objective text and cleared-state checks. All exported rows name a same-id MissionWave. A missing StoryMissionWave or MissionWave makes Story_GetBattleLayout return EGameBattlePair::Invalid (255); the demo-task chain instead returns no task. The supplied export has no MissionWave row for STMSN_06090S.

Id_BattleTalkSet.simple: Battle-talk sets attached to this wave.
Id_BattleTalkSet.technical: TArray<FName> (row +0x30), with ten slots in every exported row. FBattleStoryState_Fight reads the cached current wave: None is skipped; a set with no non-None BattleTalkSet::ValueType entries is queued on entry, once per set, while a set with at least one condition is queued in Tick only when battle talk is enabled, each non-None condition passes EvaluateLog and Success_GreaterThanEquals/Success_LessThanEquals against its threshold, and the set has not already been queued. BattleStoryNotify368/360 resolve the wave by MissionRetryCount (not necessarily wave 0) and preload the referenced sets’ non-None cue sheets and battle-talk image names. Array order is preserved; unresolved set ids are skipped.

notes: Exported -2 occurs once (STMSN_06089S). No consumer branches on -2 specifically: it follows the negative fallbacks in Story_GetPlayableCharacterIndex and Story_GetBattleLayout, and Story_HasPlayableCharacterIndex is false.
Both exported FName arrays keep fixed lengths (three ally slots and ten battle-talk-set slots); None is an empty sentinel at a retained index, not array truncation.

93 exported rows; only one StoryMissionWaveDataTable export was found across the datatables and by-character shards, with no localisation variants. Community wiki field descriptions are Unknown placeholders, not evidence.

Several first-wave helpers read Id_StoryMissionWave[0] or GetData()[0] without validating Num, and different finders pass different bCheckNone flags; empty or None wave ids are therefore not uniformly guarded.

STMSN_09112M has no row under its own id; its Id_StoryMissionWave points at STMSN_09112M_01 through _04. In the supplied exports, STMSN_06090S.Id_MissionWave has no matching MissionWave row and STMSN_06090S_ALLY_01 has no matching MissionCharacter row; STMSN_03036M lists STMSN_03036M_01_02 under Id_BattleTalkSet although that id is a BattleTalk row rather than a BattleTalkSet row. Treat these as export/data anomalies; the runtime lookups skip unresolved ids or return invalid/no task.

Behavior here is reconstructed from static C++ and retail layout pins. status/ records byte-match verdicts for several consumers (including Story_GetPlayableCharacterIndex, Story_HasPlayableCharacterIndex, Story_GetBattleLayout, SetupStory and the story fight state Enter/Tick), but not every path; no retail Blueprint or live-runtime trace was available for this review.

usages.detail: Loads StoryMissionWaveDataTable into the StoryMissionWaveDataTables lookup array.
Declares the +0x8E0 table array used by every StoryMissionWave row finder.
Story_GetPlayableCharacterIndex reads the first wave and applies the explicit/one-ally fallback.
Story_ResolveDemoLaunch resolves the playable index, stores it in the request, and indexes the first wave’s ally array for the player battle slot; -1 routes to character select.
Story_GetBattleLayout counts the selected wave’s allies/enemies but uses the first wave’s PlayableCharacterIndex for the single-ally fallback.
Mission-task lookup walks StoryMissionWave -> MissionWave -> MissionTaskLottery -> first MissionTask.
Story_GetMissionAllyCharacters resolves ally rows from one or all waves, deduplicates them, and puts the playable slot first within each wave.
Story_FindMissionAllyCharacter resolves a validated ally index from the first wave.
The story fight state queues the cached wave’s unconditional battle-talk sets on entry and its satisfied conditional sets in Tick.
SetupBattleCharacterEntries builds player, NPC ally and enemy entries from the cached StoryMissionWave and its linked MissionWave.
Battle-story notify hooks resolve the RetryCount-selected wave to preload battle-talk cue sheets and talk images.
SetupStoryMission forwards the mission and wave arrays into the battle task-system cache; GetStoryMissionWave exposes the current wave.
SetupStory stores StoryMissionWaves and selects StoryMissionWave = InStoryWaves[RetryCount].
Character select loads first-wave allies and uses the resolved playable index to decide whether the player chooses one.
Mission select collects allies across all waves for the playable-character icons.
Mission info resolves the first wave’s MissionWave and MissionOrder for the win-condition text.
Character-select widgets gate focus/idle animations on Story_HasPlayableCharacterIndex.
